bio.en: Dan Shipper is co-founder and CEO of Every, a company at the bleeding edge of AI adoption, and returns to predict where AI and work are heading after his earlier correct call on Claude Code.
bio.zh: Dan Shipper 是 Every 的联合创始人兼 CEO，一家处于 AI 应用最前沿的公司，继此前准确预言 Claude Code 后，他再度做客预测 AI 与工作将走向何方。

summary.en: Dan pushes back on “AI jobpocalypse” panic, arguing he's bullish on PMs and full-stack designers because models commoditize yesterday's competence while humans create something new. He predicts work bifurcates into everyone having at least one agent and most work happening inside environments like Codex or Claude Code. The conversation covers why creativity becomes more valuable and why he's both extremely AI-pilled and bullish on humans.
summary.zh: Dan 反驳“AI 就业末日”的恐慌，认为他看好 PM 和全栈设计师，因为模型把“昨天的人的能力”商品化，而人类创造新东西。他预测工作将一分为二：人人至少有一个智能体，且多数工作在 Codex 或 Claude Code 这类环境中发生。对话涵盖为何创造力更值钱，以及他为何既极度 AI 化又看好人类。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: The last time you were on this podcast, you had this hot take that people were sleeping on Claude Code. You were so unbelievably right. The premise of this episode is we're going to go through what else you predict will happen.
turns.zh: 上次你上这个播客时，你有一个很热门的观点，认为人们在克劳德·代码上睡觉。你说得太对了，令人难以置信。本集的前提是我们将了解您预测会发生的其他情况。

turns.speaker: Dan Shipper
turns.en: The AI jobpocalypse is not really a thing. I am super, super bullish on PMs and full stack designers.
turns.zh: 人工智能就业末日并不是真正的事情。我非常非常看好产品经理和全栈设计师。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: You guys are hiring, doubled in people in the past year, which is not what people would've expected from a company that is so AI-forward.
turns.zh: 你们正在招聘，人数在过去一年翻了一番，这不是人们对一家如此人工智能先进的公司所期望的。

turns.speaker: Dan Shipper
turns.en: I'm simultaneously extremely AI pilled and very bullish on humans. Automation is a lot. Every agent needs a human. We have so much automation, so much AI, and I also work way more.
turns.zh: 我对人工智能非常着迷，同时又非常看好人类。自动化有很多。每个代理都需要一个人。我们有如此多的自动化、如此多的人工智能，而且我的工作量也更多了。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Creativity, it just feels like it's going to be more and more valuable to stand out from all the slot that people are shipping and launching constantly.
turns.zh: 创造力，感觉从人们不断推出和推出的所有老虎机中脱颖而出会变得越来越有价值。

turns.speaker: Dan Shipper
turns.en: What models do in general is they make yesterday's human competence cheap. And so it becomes commoditized. It's not valuable anymore. What humans do is we go in there and we're like, "Yeah, we have all this frozen human competence from yesterday. How do I use this to make something new and interesting?"
turns.zh: 模型的一般作用是让昨天的人类能力变得廉价。因此它变得商品化。它已经不值钱了。人类所做的就是我们走进去，然后我们会想，“是的，我们从昨天起就拥有了所有这些冻结的人类能力。我如何利用它来创造一些新的、有趣的东西？”

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: What are some predictions for how the way we work is going to change?
turns.zh: 对于我们的工作方式将如何改变有哪些预测？

turns.speaker: Dan Shipper
turns.en: It's going to bifurcate in two main ways. One is everyone's going to have at least one agent that they talk to that they can offload work to. Second is that most of the work that you do is actually going to happen on your computer in an environment like Codex or Claude Cowork.
turns.zh: 它将以两种主要方式分裂。一是每个人都至少有一位可以与之交谈的代理人，可以将工作分担给他们。其次，您所做的大部分工作实际上都会在 Codex 或 Claude Cowork 等环境中的计算机上进行。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: What you're predicting here is the SaaS tools will run within Codex or Claude Code.
turns.zh: 您在这里预测的是 SaaS 工具将在 Codex 或 Claude Code 中运行。

turns.speaker: Dan Shipper
turns.en: I think the SaaSpocalypse is dumb. I would buy SaaS stocks right now. What agents do is increase the number of users of SaaS, not get rid of it.
turns.zh: 我认为 SaaS 末日是愚蠢的。我现在会购买 SaaS 股票。代理商所做的是增加SaaS的用户数量，而不是摆脱它。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: A lot of people are moving to CLI and trying to work from the terminal.
turns.zh: 许多人正在转向 CLI 并尝试在终端上工作。

turns.speaker: Dan Shipper
turns.en: We speed ran the CLI era. It was nice while it lasted, but I think CLIs are over.
turns.zh: 我们加速了 CLI 时代。虽然它持续的时间很好，但我认为 CLI 已经结束了。

turns.speaker: Dan Shipper
turns.en: Thank you. I really appreciate the introduction. And yeah, I think one of the things about predicting the future or the way that we think about predicting the future at Every is that what you don't want to do is prognosticate. What you want to do instead is just live in it together. So everybody at Every is an AI early adopter. We're almost 30 people now. I think when we did our interview, we were 15, so we've doubled in size in the last year. I like to experiment. I'm very curious and I'm super all-in on AI." And what that does, I think, is it creates this little pocket of the future where we're all living in it together and we get to be a little bit further ahead because at any other company, there's a mix of people. (00:05:31): There's early adopters. There's the middle of the pack people and there's people who are very anti. And another thing that happens, which is really cool is we get to, because of our role reviewing models and being a little bit of a pacemaker in AI, we get access to stuff before it comes out. So we get to beta test and alpha test and help steer the direction of where things are going a little bit, which is very, very cool. And so when I think about predicting the future, it's actually, when you create an environment like that, it's actually just about noticing what's going on. I think a core part of it too is writing about it. I think articulating what you're noticing, articulating the future brings it about in this way that makes it real for you and your team and then anybody else who's like on the internet who's reading it. (00:06:24): And so the Claude Code thing, it's this very organic thing where, for us, we tried Claude Code when it came out. That's our job. We tried all the new stuff from the model companies and at the time, it was like a little bit early, but right around I think like Sonnet 3.5 or Sonnet 3.7, we were testing that to do our vibe check on it and we were like, "Holy shit, this is crazy." They got rid of the code editor. And so from that point on, we just basically, at this point now we run like six software products internally. At that time we ran maybe two or three. And from that point on, we just started shifting to a world where no one was looking at the code. Everybody was talking to their computer in English, using Claude Code in the terminal. (00:07:19): And so I was able to see like, "Ooh, this is starting to happen." And then because my job is a little bit to just push and play with stuff, I was like, "I wonder if I could use this for my writing. How could I do that?" And then it just starts to unfold and you're like, "Okay, this is not ready yet, but it's obviously useful for me." One of the things that we talk about internally is what I call the reach test, which is like, when you wake up in the morning, do you reach for it organically?

turns.en: One of my favorite questions, because I think if you look at the benchmarks, you're just looking at, okay, yeah, AI is going to just take all of our jobs, basically. It becomes a operating system for how you do all of your work, whether that's your email, the documents you create, all that stuff. It's going to be on that kind of surface. That's becoming the clear competitive landscape. (00:12:37): I want to go in order of those two. So the first one is you're going to have agents you delegate to probably in Slack, but anywhere. First thing that's interesting about that one is it's not clear what the architecture is going to be like for that. Is everyone going to have an agent? Is every team going to have an agent? Is it going to be just one agent? Do agents specialize? Is there this parallel shadow org chart? And when OpenClaw first came out, everyone internally at Every adopted it and I was very convinced that it would be everyone has their own agent and there's some really interesting things about that world of a parallel org chart. Agents in that world become little reflections of you, which is really cool and really interesting. It's like if you ever ... Did you ever read the Golden Compass?
turns.zh: 我最喜欢的问题之一，因为我认为如果你看一下基准，你就会发现，好吧，是的，人工智能基本上会取代我们所有的工作。 Meter 有一个非常酷的基准测试，它可以衡量最新模型可以自主执行任务多长时间，就像，哦，它可以，它叫什么？哦，神话预览，大家都担心的大人择模型，它可以以 50% 的准确率完成 17 个小时的任务。就像，天啊，这太疯狂了。我认为这是真的。这是事实，模型的进步正在呈指数级增长。我的经验和感觉是，一年后我们回顾起来，我们实际上还有很多工作要做。尽管模型在工作方面做得越来越好，但人类还有很多工作要做。这里有一个非常有趣的悖论。我对一年后工作将如何改变或你将如何工作的主要预测是，它将在两个主要方面出现分歧，即你如何使用代理。 (00:11:41)：一是你要做的事情，我想五年前我们在考虑人工智能工作如何运作时就想到了你会做的事情，即每个人至少在他们的公司里，至少有一个可以与之交谈的代理人，可以做工作，可以将工作交给他们。我们将讨论它的外观，但它本质上就像 OpenClaw。其次，您所做的大部分工作实际上都会在您的计算机上、在 Codex 或 Claude Cowork 等环境中进行。它成为了...的操作系统，它成为了你如何完成所有工作的操作系统，无论是你的电子邮件、你创建的文档还是所有这些东西。它将在那种表面上。这正在成为清晰的竞争格局。 (00:12:37)：我想按照这两个的顺序进行。所以第一个是你可能会在 Slack 中，但在任何地方都有你委托的代理。第一件有趣的事情是，目前尚不清楚其架构会是什么样子。每个人都会有代理吗？每个球队都会有经纪人吗？难道只有一名代理人吗？代理商专业吗？有这个平行的影子组织结构图吗？当 OpenClaw 第一次问世时，Every 内部的每个人都采用了它，我非常确信每个人都有自己的代理，并且关于并行组织结构图的世界有一些非常有趣的事情。那个世界里的特工变成了你的小倒影，这真的很酷也很有趣。就像如果你曾经……你读过《黄金罗盘》吗？

turns.en: That's a little part of your soul. I really think that's what it looked like was happening. And so I was very into personal agents and I have completely flipped and I really think that the model, for now, is going to be a super agent, like one agent for the entire company and you're starting to see this in some companies. So Shopify very famously has one, Ramp has one now and I think there's some really interesting reasons for that. I actually still think that the personal agent thing is coming, but what we found is there's all this hype with OpenClaw. Everyone's like, "I'm going to set it up. It's so cool," or whatever. And then everyone realizes it's like way too much work. This thing breaks all the time. I got to fumble around with it. I got to be able to SSH into my server and like blah, blah, blah. And most people, to do work at least, just don't want to spend that time, or can't. (00:14:38): And the fundamental, underlying thing that drives that is whether it's OpenClaw or any other harness, in order for an AI agent to be useful right now, it really needs a human who cares about it. It really needs a human personal connection with someone who's watching what it does and makes sure that it's doing the right thing and that it's useful for people. And the minute you sever that connection, so the minute someone's like, "Ah, I don't want to maintain this dumb OpenClaw," is the minute the agent is not really that useful anymore. And that's why I think it has started to shift to a more one agent per company model because for now, the ideal is you basically set up a forward deployed engineer or someone with that profile who's responsible for making sure that that agent is working for the whole company and then maybe you have some little team agents. (00:15:34): And I think as the models get better at being more independent, that will shift down and it'll be more likely that we'll have more personal agents because we won't have to fuck around with all the internals. But the model that I see working for us and for a lot of other companies, including the model companies, the model companies themselves are starting to see this, is when it comes to the like async agents, it's really a, you have one agent at the top that's like doing, sometimes it's everything. A lot of times it's a particular job that you've decided that everyone in the company needs an agent for, like data requests. And then I think it starts at the top and then it starts to trickle down, where you may get more specialized agents and teams and all that kind of stuff. And the mechanism is agents need people who care about them.
turns.zh: 那是你灵魂的一小部分。我真的认为事情就是这样发生的。所以我非常喜欢个人经纪人，我已经彻底转变了，我真的认为目前的模式将是一个超级经纪人，就像整个公司的一个经纪人，你开始在一些公司看到这种情况。 Shopify 有一个非常出名的产品，Ramp 现在也有一个，我认为这有一些非常有趣的原因。事实上，我仍然认为个人代理即将到来，但我们发现 OpenClaw 受到了如此大的炒作。每个人都会说，“我要去设置它。这太酷了”，或者其他什么。然后每个人都意识到这工作量太大了。这东西总是坏掉。我得摸索它。我必须能够通过 SSH 连接到我的服务器，诸如此类。而大多数人，至少在工作中，只是不想花时间，或者不能花时间。 (00:14:38)：驱动这一点的根本因素是，无论是 OpenClaw 还是任何其他工具，为了让人工智能代理现在发挥作用，它确实需要一个关心它的人。它确实需要与关注它所做的事情并确保它做正确的事情并且对人们有用的人建立个人联系。当你切断连接的那一刻，所以当有人说，“啊，我不想维护这个愚蠢的 OpenClaw”的那一刻，代理就不再那么有用了。这就是为什么我认为它已经开始转向每个公司多一个代理的模式，因为目前，理想的情况是你基本上设置一名前沿部署工程师或具有该配置文件的人员，负责确保该代理为整个公司工作，然后也许你有一些小团队代理。 (00:15:34)：我认为，随着模型变得更加独立，这种情况将会发生变化，我们更有可能拥有更多的个人代理，因为我们不必再处理所有的内部事务。但我认为对我们和许多其他公司（包括模型公司）有效的模型，模型公司本身也开始看到这一点，当涉及到异步代理时，这实际上是一个，你在顶部有一个代理，就像在做，有时它就是一切。很多时候，您决定公司中的每个人都需要代理来完成一项特定的工作，例如数据请求。然后我认为它从顶部开始，然后开始向下渗透，你可能会得到更专业的代理人和团队以及所有类似的东西。其机制是代理人需要关心他们的人。

turns.speaker: Dan Shipper
turns.en: I'm so excited about this one. I think it's the coolest thing. So basically what happened was Anthropic realized at some point that, with Claude Code, if you put an agent on your computer and it runs on your computer, it has access to everything that you have access to. It uses the terminal, so it has basically superpowered access to it. And not only that, these agents really understand how to use the terminal because there's so much content online about that and it created this super powerful coding paradigm, which is Anthropic was really doing it first. OpenAI, for a while, was, in my opinion, very, very behind on this and then, in my opinion, has surpassed them recently. It's really interesting, but they were very early on this. When people were still thinking about coding agents or coding models as being really pair programmers, they were among the first to be like, no, and do it successfully. (00:19:17): There were people before them, like Devin, who, I think, had the big cloud environment and OpenAI tried this too, but the real adoption seems to have happened when you put it on your computer. So they figured that out and then I think they figured out, along with their community, that once you have a coding agent on your computer that can build anything, it's actually really good for any kind of work you want to do. And people started just hacking Claude Code, essentially, to do all of their work. Anthropic then built Cowork, which is a little bit of a nicer wrapping around Claude Code, but is fundamentally the same thing. And then I think OpenAI made a couple of different bets, but their main bet on a programming agent was the earlier versions of Codex were very technical and they were super smart, but they were a little bit autistic. (00:20:13): It was a little hard to ... They didn't quite get what you meant. They got exactly what you said. And I think maybe like three or four months ago, around the time that they launched 5.3, they started to move in this direction of, "Oh no, we get it. This model is fast. It's really good for general purpose, knowledge work type tasks." And then they launched the Codex desktop app. And I think the Codex desktop app takes ... If you look at all the lessons that Anthropic learned, they went from Claude code to Cowork and you can see that in the tabs on the Anthropic desktop app UI. I think OpenAI was just like, "We see where this is going. Let's just skip to that." And so I think Codex right now, this is a horse race. They're going to have different positions, but I think Codex right now, it's my daily driver. (00:21:06): I spend all my time in it, basically. I flip to Claude every once in a while, but I think they're getting the paradigm right. And it's clear to me that whoever is in the lead, because again, I think it'll change. Whoever's in the lead, it feels very obvious to me that all of the work that you do is going to be in one of those surfaces where, for example, when I'm writing a document, Codex has a browser in the app. It has an in-app browser. And when I'm writing a document, I just go into one of my Codex threads, which I have one thread for every project, and I just open the in-app browser, I go to the document, I usually do it in Proof, which is this online markdown editor I built. (00:21:49): And then I just have Codex running and watching me in Proof and Codex can see what I'm doing. I can see what Codex is doing. It's all in one place, which is an extension of the same thing that made Claude Code work really well originally. And I basically feel like I have this parallel work buddy that not only can it respond and write in the document, but then it can go do research, it can use my computer to basically do anything that I can do on my computer and that's incredibly powerful. And I do this with everything. I've been at inbox zero for 10 days straight now, which if you know me, is crazy. I'm never like this, and that's because I literally just have Codex gather all my emails with Quora, which is our email agent. And then it renders a little page, and I think I showed you this at the Anthropic event. It renders a little page and I just monologue into it and just talk out each email. (00:22:49): I'm like, "Okay, go research this. Oh, here's a question from our lawyers. Can you go collect all of the documents from the last four years and then put them into a report and send them?" And it just does it. And so all the stuff that I would procrastinate on, I don't really procrastinate on anymore. And so I feel like there's this, for a long time, I thought too that the optimal experience of AI was going to be take AI and put it in a browser. And I think the reverse is actually starting to happen and be really, really valuable in a way that I did not expect, which is take the AI agent that you use all the time on your computer and put a browser in it so it can see everything you're doing. And that is just like a magical combination that I think is very uncommon now. You can't even do this in Claude Code because they don't let you browse external websites inside of Claude Code. So it's very uncommon now, but I think it will be super common in a year.
turns.zh: 我对此感到非常兴奋。我认为这是最酷的事情。所以基本上发生的事情是 Anthropic 在某个时刻意识到，通过 Claude Code，如果你在你的计算机上放置一个代理并且它在你的计算机上运行，​​它就可以访问你有权访问的所有内容。它使用终端，因此它基本上具有超级访问权限。不仅如此，这些代理真正了解如何使用终端，因为网上有很多关于终端的内容，并且它创建了这个超级强大的编码范例，这是 Anthropic 真正首先做到的。在我看来，OpenAI 有一段时间在这方面非常非常落后，但在我看来，最近已经超越了他们。这真的很有趣，但他们很早就开始这样做了。当人们仍然认为编码代理或编码模型是真正的结对程序员时，他们是最先表示“不”并成功做到这一点的人之一。 (00:19:17)：在他们之前有人，比如 Devin，我认为他们拥有大型云环境，OpenAI 也尝试过这一点，但真正的采用似乎是当你把它放在你的计算机上时发生的。所以他们发现了这一点，然后我认为他们和他们的社区一起发现，一旦你的计算机上有了一个可以构建任何东西的编码代理，它实际上对你想做的任何类型的工作都有好处。人们开始只是通过破解 Claude Code 来完成他们所有的工作。 Anthropic 随后构建了 Cowork，它是 Claude Code 的更好的包装，但本质上是一样的。然后我认为 OpenAI 做了几个不同的赌注，但他们对编程代理的主要赌注是 Codex 的早期版本非常技术化，而且他们非常聪明，但他们有点自闭。 (00:20:13)：有点难……他们不太明白你的意思。他们完全明白你所说的。我想也许就像三四个月前，大约在他们推出 5.3 的时候，他们开始朝这个方向发展，“哦，不，我们明白了。这个模型很快。它非常适合通用的知识工作类型任务。”然后他们推出了 Codex 桌面应用程序。我认为 Codex 桌面应用程序需要......如果你看看 Anthropic 学到的所有经验教训，他们从 Claude 代码到 Cowork，你可以在 Anthropic 桌面应用程序 UI 的选项卡中看到这一点。我认为 OpenAI 就像是，“我们知道这会发生什么。让我们跳到那个。”所以我认为现在 Codex 是一场赛马。他们会有不同的职位，但我认为 Codex 现在是我的日常司机。 (00:21:06)：基本上我所有的时间都花在了上面。我偶尔会转向克劳德，但我认为他们的范例是正确的。我很清楚，无论谁处于领先地位，因为我再次认为情况将会改变。无论谁处于领先地位，对我来说很明显的是，您所做的所有工作都将在其中一个界面中进行，例如，当我编写文档时，Codex 在应用程序中有一个浏览器。它有一个应用内浏览器。当我编写文档时，我只需进入我的 Codex 线程之一，每个项目都有一个线程，然后我只需打开应用内浏览器，转到文档，我通常在 Proof 中执行此操作，这是我构建的在线 Markdown 编辑器。 (00:21:49)：然后我就让 Codex 运行并在 Proof 中观察我，Codex 可以看到我在做什么。我可以看到 Codex 在做什么。一切都集中在一个地方，这是 Claude Code 最初运行良好的同一事物的延伸。我基本上觉得我有一个并行的工作伙伴，它不仅可以响应并在文档中写入，而且还可以进行研究，它可以使用我的计算机基本上做我可以在计算机上做的任何事情，这是非常强大的。我对所有事情都这样做。我已经连续 10 天收件箱为零，如果你了解我的话，这太疯狂了。我从来不会这样，那是因为我实际上只是让 Codex 通过 Quora（我们的电子邮件代理）收集我的所有电子邮件。然后它会呈现一个小页面，我想我在 Anthropic 活动中向您展示了这一点。它呈现一个小页面，我只是在其中独白并说出每封电子邮件。 (00:22:49)：我想，“好吧，去研究一下。哦，这是我们律师的问题。你能收集过去四年的所有文件，然后将它们放入报告中并发送吗？”它就是这么做的。所以所有我会拖延的事情，我都不再拖延了。所以我觉得很长一段时间以来，我也认为人工智能的最佳体验是将人工智能放入浏览器中。我认为相反的情况实际上已经开始发生，并且以一种我没有想到的方式非常非常有价值，那就是使用你一直在计算机上使用的人工智能代理，并在其中放置一个浏览器，这样它就可以看到你正在做的一切。这就像一个神奇的组合，我认为现在非常罕见。您甚至无法在 Claude Code 中执行此操作，因为它们不允许您在 Claude Code 内浏览外部网站。所以现在这种情况很不常见，但我认为一年后就会非常常见。

turns.en: That is one really important second order effect of this is ... Okay, so yeah, I'm using Proof or really any website, maybe PostHog or whatever, and I'm doing it inside of my agent and the agent has access to the website. So, it has access to everything that I have access to, and it has access to my whole computer. When I run the agent on that website, I'm using my tokens. I'm not using the vendor's tokens, I'm not using the app's tokens. And so, it puts SaaS back in this place where yeah, you want to make it friendly for an agent and everyone's got a CLI now, you want to make the HTML really usable. You want to make sure that anything that happens in the CLI shows up for the user immediately, all that kind of stuff. There are a lot of issues to deal with. But once you do that, you actually don't really need to think about having an AI surface that's primarily going to be the thing that users use in the sense that you don't need to build an agent necessarily into your product. (00:25:03): I think you can, and there's another really interesting bifurcation of this that we should talk about, which is that having two agents is better than one. But I think for now there's this really cool thing where with Proof, for example, anyone who uses it, I don't pay for tokens because they bring their AI to Proof. And so, it changes what you build as a SaaS company and you build it now for both humans and agents to use at the same time, and it changes your margins back to, well, I don't really have to pay for tokens anymore because the user's going to bring AI.
turns.zh: 这是一个非常重要的二阶效应……好吧，是的，我正在使用 Proof 或任何网站，也许是 PostHog 或其他什么，而且我是在我的代理内部执行此操作，并且代理可以访问该网站。因此，它可以访问我可以访问的所有内容，并且可以访问我的整个计算机。当我在该网站上运行代理时，我正在使用我的令牌。我没有使用供应商的令牌，也没有使用应用程序的令牌。因此，它让 SaaS 回到了这个位置，是的，你想让它对代理友好，现在每个人都有 CLI，你想让 HTML 真正可用。您希望确保 CLI 中发生的任何事情都能立即向用户显示，诸如此类。有很多问题需要处理。但一旦你这样做了，你实际上并不需要考虑拥有一个主要供用户使用的人工智能界面，因为你不需要在你的产品中构建一个代理。 (00:25:03)：我认为你可以，而且我们应该讨论另一个非常有趣的分歧，那就是拥有两个代理比一个代理更好。但我认为现在有一件非常酷的事情，例如，对于 Proof，任何使用它的人，我都不需要支付代币费用，因为他们将人工智能带到了 Proof。因此，它改变了你作为 SaaS 公司所构建的内容，你现在构建它供人类和代理同时使用，并且它将你的利润改变回，嗯，我真的不需要再支付代币了，因为用户将带来人工智能。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: So, I think this is a huge deal. So, what you're describing here is more and more work that we do, more and more professional work, is it just going to happen within Codex or Claude Code? Where does Cursor fit into this? Is there potential there?
turns.zh: 所以，我认为这是一件大事。那么，你在这里描述的是我们所做的越来越多的工作，越来越专业的工作，这会发生在 Codex 或 Claude Code 中吗？ Cursor 在哪里适合这个？那里有潜力吗？

turns.speaker: Dan Shipper
turns.en: That's a good question. I think that Cursor sees a lot of the same stuff, and in some ways they have some of the same stuff but it's better. I think that Cursor's cloud implementation is better than either OpenAIs or Anthropics and is more advanced, and I think that Cursor has at least so far more distinctly chosen a lane. They're more distinctly choosing to be for programmers, and that may limit how far they get in here. I think the definition programmer is expanding enough that they'll have a big market, but I don't know that they're going to jump into like, "Okay, use this to make a slide deck," or whatever. But it is really clear that every model company is starting to realize how important it is to have a harness to get the most out of the model. And so, where all the platforms are moving is to a world where you're not just doing prompt and response. (00:26:51): When you call the model on the OpenAI platform, the Anthropic platform, they're literally running the model on a computer that is in the cloud that they run and then giving you the result out of it. And they know that in order to get the best results of the model they need to offer that. And so, you see Anthropic's got cloud managed agents. OpenAI does not have a response yet, but I assume that that's going to happen. And now Cursor was just essentially acquired by SpaceX. It's not like a full acquisition, but it's close. So, I think people are starting to realize I can't just do the model part of it, I have to have this harness above it. And I think the ultimate form of that harness is like I can do any kind of knowledge work. Cursor itself feels like one of the things that it's going to be a hard decision for them whether to stay just for coders or not.
turns.zh: 这是个好问题。我认为 Cursor 看到了很多相同的东西，在某些方面他们有一些相同的东西，但更好。我认为 Cursor 的云实现比 OpenAIs 或 Anthropics 都更好，而且更先进，而且我认为 Cursor 至少到目前为止已经更明确地选择了一条路线。他们更明确地选择成为程序员，这可能会限制他们在这里能走多远。我认为程序员的定义已经足够扩展，他们将拥有一个很大的市场，但我不知道他们会跳入“好吧，用它来制作幻灯片”之类的想法。但很明显，每个模型公司都开始意识到拥有一个安全带来充分利用模型是多么重要。因此，所有平台正在走向一个不仅仅是进行提示和响应的世界。 (00:26:51)：当你在 OpenAI 平台、Anthropic 平台上调用模型时，他们实际上是在他们运行的云中的计算机上运行模型，然后为你提供结果。他们知道，为了获得模型的最佳结果，他们需要提供这一点。因此，您会看到 Anthropic 拥有云管理代理。 OpenAI 尚未做出回应，但我认为这将会发生。现在 Cursor 基本上被 SpaceX 收购了。这不像完全收购，但也很接近了。所以，我认为人们开始意识到我不能只做其中的模型部分，我必须在它上面放置这个安全带。我认为这种控制的最终形式就像我可以做任何类型的知识工作。光标本身感觉就像是他们要做出一个艰难决定是否只为程序员保留的事情之一。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: So, if people building products that aren't OpenAI or Anthropic, if this proves to be true, the prediction here is they're going to be using your product over time inside of one of these agents. Is there something you would do if you were one of those companies to prepare for that future?
turns.zh: 因此，如果人们构建的产品不是 OpenAI 或 Anthropic，如果这被证明是正确的，那么这里的预测是，随着时间的推移，他们将在这些代理之一中使用您的产品。如果您是这些公司之一，您会做些什么来为未来做准备吗？

turns.speaker: Dan Shipper
turns.en: I would just prepare for that. So for example, every more classic piece of productivity software, whether it's Slack, or Word docs, or PowerPoints or whatever, it's really mostly meant for a human to use. And now people are doing CLI so it's meant for an agent to use independently of a human. And we're moving into this new paradigm, I think, where the human and the agent are on the same piece of work together, and they're both doing things, and I need to have visibility into what the agent is doing, the agent has to have visibility into what I'm doing. We have to go back and forth in this seamless way. And the kind of software that you make for that is going to be very different. So for example, there's a lot of stuff that Proof doesn't have. I don't have to have a lot of the Word document formatting, or page breaks, or making tables or whatever, because the agent just does it. I don't need to worry about that, it can do all the formatting for me. (00:29:03): So, you can make the products a lot simpler and faster to start than the legacy products are. And then, there's all these other affordances that you need to start to have because the way agents interact with software is very different. So for example, agents can do a lot at once. They can just do a billion different things to your document, or your slide deck, or your code base or whatever, and how you display that to the user is going to be very different than the way you might display a human being concurrent in your document and doing stuff. You need approval, you need a inbox that summarizes, "Here's all the stuff that's going to happen," or has happened. You need logs and the ability to roll it back real quick. (00:29:46): So, there's all those kinds of considerations that change the actual product, and then the underlying UX of it or the underlying infrastructure you need is different too, because agents can make a billion requests in three seconds. So, how are you going to deal with that? This is exactly why GitHub is having problems right now because the number of people using GitHub is skyrocketing exponentially and it's really just people's agencies in GitHub. So, I think it's this whole new world that is just starting, you're just starting to see a little peek of it, but there's so many cool things about it. So for example, in Proof and some of our other products too, when someone has a problem they don't email support. Their agent sends a bug report, and an agent bug report is way better than a human bug report. It has like, "Here's exactly what I did, here's the exact repro steps, here's like ..." (00:30:40): Proof is open source so, "Here's what I think is going on in the code base." And then we just get that, it becomes a GitHub issue, and then we can just send off an agent to fix it. And you can't do that with everything but it's so much better, and you can see the glimmers of this very fast closed loop between I ran into something, a paper cut, a little feature I want, a little bug, and my agent just goes off and talks to the company agent and then the company agent just goes and fixes it. That I think is incredibly cool.
turns.zh: 我只是为此做好准备。例如，每一个更经典的生产力软件，无论是 Slack、Word 文档、PowerPoint 等等，它实际上主要是供人类使用的。现在人们正在使用 CLI，因此它意味着代理可以独立于人类使用。我认为，我们正在进入这种新的范式，人类和代理一起从事同一工作，他们都在做事情，我需要了解代理正在做什么，代理也必须了解我正在做什么。我们必须以这种无缝的方式来回进行。为此而开发的软件类型将会非常不同。例如，有很多东西是 Proof 所没有的。我不需要进行大量的 Word 文档格式设置、分页符或制作表格等工作，因为代理会完成这些工作。我不需要担心这一点，它可以为我完成所有格式设置。 (00:29:03)：因此，您可以使产品比旧产品更简单、更快速地启动。然后，您需要开始拥有所有其他可供性，因为代理与软件交互的方式非常不同。例如，代理可以同时做很多事情。他们可以对你的文档、幻灯片、代码库等执行十亿种不同的操作，而你向用户显示这些操作的方式将与你在文档中显示人类并发执行操作的方式有很大不同。您需要批准，您需要一个收件箱来总结“这是将要发生或已经发生的所有事情”。您需要日志以及快速回滚日志的能力。 (00:29:46)：所以，所有这些考虑因素都会改变实际产品，然后它的底层用户体验或您需要的底层基础设施也不同，因为代理可以在三秒钟内发出十亿个请求。那么，你打算如何处理呢？这正是 GitHub 目前遇到问题的原因，因为使用 GitHub 的人数正在呈指数级增长，而且实际上只是 GitHub 中的人们的代理机构。所以，我认为这个全新的世界才刚刚开始，你才刚刚开始看到它的一小部分，但它有很多很酷的东西。例如，在 Proof 和我们的一些其他产品中，当有人遇到问题时，他们不会发送电子邮件支持。他们的代理发送错误报告，代理错误报告比人工错误报告要好得多。它就像是，“这正是我所做的，这是确切的重现步骤，就像......”（00:30:40）：证明是开源的，所以，“这就是我认为代码库中正在发生的事情。”然后我们就明白了，它变成了 GitHub 问题，然后我们可以派一个代理来修复它。你不能对所有事情都做到这一点，但它好多了，你可以看到这个非常快速的闭环的闪光，在我遇到一些东西，一个剪纸，一个我想要的小功能，一个小错误，我的代理就离开并与公司代理交谈，然后公司代理就去修复它。我认为这非常酷。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: So, as a part of this that a lot of people are moving to CLI and trying to work from the terminal, is part of this prediction that people shift away from that and back to actual UX with agents-
turns.zh: 因此，作为其中的一部分，许多人正在转向 CLI 并尝试在终端上工作，这是人们从 CLI 转向使用代理的实际 UX 的预测的一部分 -

turns.speaker: Dan Shipper
turns.en: Oh, yeah.
turns.zh: 哦，是的。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: ... running alongside them?
turns.zh: ……和他们一起跑？

turns.speaker: Dan Shipper
turns.en: CLIs are over. We speed ran the CLI era. It was nice while it lasted, but I think it's pretty clear ... Sorry. It's not that CLIs are going to completely go away. Obviously they've been around for the last like 30 years, or 40 years or 50 years or whatever. They will continue to be around. And I think there is this moment when Claude Code was so popular, or when Claude Code was really starting to gain in popularity that people were like, "The thing that's working is the fact that it's the CLI," and I don't think that's what it is. And when you move into an actual UI for this, you start to realize we made GUIs for a reason, and it's just nicer to be in a GUI, and you can get all the same benefits inside of a GUI, especially for non-programmer work. But I would estimate that definitely the majority of the technical people inside of Every are not using CLIs anymore as their main work surface. (00:32:27): I think a lot of programmers are still flipping into it every once in a while, but it's more or less they're using Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, that kind of thing.
turns.zh: CLI 已经结束。我们加速了 CLI 时代。持续的时候很好，但我认为它很清楚......抱歉。这并不是说 CLI 将完全消失。显然，它们已经存在了 30 年、40 年、50 年等等。他们将继续存在。我认为，当 Claude Code 如此受欢迎时，或者当 Claude Code 真正开始流行时，人们会说，“真正起作用的是 CLI，”我认为事实并非如此。当您为此进入实际的 UI 时，您开始意识到我们制作 GUI 是有原因的，并且在 GUI 中更好，并且您可以在 GUI 中获得所有相同的好处，特别是对于非程序员工作。但我估计，Every 内部的大多数技术人员肯定不再使用 CLI 作为他们的主要工作界面。 (00:32:27)：我认为很多程序员仍然时不时地投入其中，但他们或多或少都在使用 Codex、Claude Code、Cursor 之类的东西。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Awesome, okay. I definitely wanted to make that part clear. So, coming back to the big picture of the prediction here, there's these two modes of work that you're anticipating. One is this super agent within a company that you chat with through Slack most likely that can go off and do work and answer questions, and then there's on your computer running Codex or Claude Code. And within that, all the work that you normally do on your computers now are going to be living within Codex or Claude Code, or maybe some third party that emerges that we're not even aware of yet.
turns.zh: 太棒了，好吧。我确实想把这部分说清楚。因此，回到这里的预测的大局，您正在期待这两种工作模式。一种是公司内的超级代理，您可以通过 Slack 与之聊天，很可能可以出去工作并回答问题，然后在您的计算机上运行 Codex 或 Claude Code。在此范围内，您现在通常在计算机上执行的所有工作都将位于 Codex 或 Claude Code 中，或者可能是一些我们尚未意识到的第三方。

turns.speaker: Dan Shipper
turns.en: Yes. And you're going to use apps inside of the internal browser of those tools.
turns.zh: 是的。您将在这些工具的内部浏览器内使用应用程序。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Wow, okay. Listening to you talk about it, it may not feel as profound as it is, because this is a big change to how we work. We don't currently have an AI that we talk to regularly in Slack, and we also don't work currently mostly in Codex or Claude Code. So, this is actually a pretty massive shift.
turns.zh: 哇，好吧。听你讲，感觉可能没有那么深刻，因为这是我们工作方式的一个很大的改变。我们目前没有在 Slack 中定期与之交谈的人工智能，而且目前我们也主要不在 Codex 或 Claude Code 中工作。所以，这实际上是一个相当巨大的转变。

turns.speaker: Dan Shipper
turns.en: I think so.
turns.zh: 我想是的。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Is there anything else along these lines before we get into our next prediction?
turns.zh: 在我们进行下一个预测之前，还有其他类似的事情吗？

turns.speaker: Dan Shipper
turns.en: Well, a few things. I'm definitely not an agent maximalist, I really think we're going to have a lot of different agents that we use. It seems pretty clear to me. And I really do think that two agents are better than one, so what's a good example? When I have Codex interact with another agent, it can give so much more context about me and what I want than I would be able to type, and it can go back and forth talking about things that would take a long time for me to express directly to an agent that you get this speed up effect when you assume that your users are using Codex, or Claude Code, or Cowork as their basic way they access your app. And a really simple example, we have this hosted OpenClaw product, which we had on waitlist. We actually had to pause it because we started taking people off the waitlist, and OpenClaw is just a very a very hard agent harness to make work. (00:34:41): It's moving so incredibly fast, and if you're like a platform for it, it's like when things break you can't fix it. It's very hard. But one of the things that we learned in that process is let's say you're building an agent product or any new software experience, what you would assume, let's say to set up an agent, is you need to build a little web interface or a little Slack workflow that asks people about, "Okay, who are you and what are you going to use this for? And what's your ideal dream outcome?" Or whatever the things you are that you would put on an onboarding checklist. (00:35:24): If instead you just make a hard line of we are only going to service users who use Codex or Cowork, what happens is you just paste a prompt into Codex or Cowork, it goes and talks to the app, and the app can be either just a regular server or it can be its own agent, and Codex has so much information about you that it can just give it. "Here's all the stuff I've been working on with Dan, here's all the ways that he might want to use this app," and then bring it back to me, and it's this very custom experience. And also for a technical product like an agent, when something goes wrong I can just tell Codex, "Go fix it." And Codex will go talk to the app and figure out what's going on for me. And so, I think the whole paradigm starts to change when you assume that everyone's got an agent and those agents are talking to other agents in this really magical and important way.
turns.zh: 嗯，有几件事。我绝对不是一个代理最大化主义者，我真的认为我们将会使用很多不同的代理。对我来说这似乎很清楚。我确实认为两个代理比一个代理更好，那么有什么好的例子呢？当我让 Codex 与另一个代理交互时，它可以提供比我能够输入的更多的关于我和我想要的内容的上下文，并且它可以来回谈论我需要很长时间才能直接向代理表达的事情，当您假设您的用户使用 Codex、Claude Code 或 Cowork 作为访问您的应用程序的基本方式时，您会得到这种加速效果。一个非常简单的例子，我们有这个托管的 OpenClaw 产品，我们已经将其列入候补名单。事实上，我们不得不暂停它，因为我们开始将人们从候补名单中剔除，而 OpenClaw 只是一个非常难以发挥作用的代理工具。 (00:34:41)：它的发展速度如此之快，如果你就像它的平台，就像事情出了问题你无法修复它一样。这很难。但我们在这个过程中学到的一件事是，假设你正在构建一个代理产品或任何新的软件体验，你会假设，假设要设置一个代理，你需要构建一个小的 Web 界面或一个小的 Slack 工作流程，询问人们：“好吧，你是谁，你打算用它做什么？你理想的梦想结果是什么？”或者无论您是什么，您都会将其列入入职清单。 (00:35:24)：如果你只是强硬地表示我们只为使用 Codex 或 Cowork 的用户提供服务，那么你只需将提示粘贴到 Codex 或 Cowork 中，它就会与应用程序对话，应用程序可以只是一个常规服务器，也可以是它自己的代理，Codex 有如此多的关于你的信息，它可以直接提供。 “这是我和 Dan 一起做的所有事情，这是他可能想要使用这个应用程序的所有方式，”然后把它带回给我，这是一种非常定制的体验。对于像代理这样的技术产品，当出现问题时，我可以告诉 Codex，“去修复它。” Codex 会与该应用程序对话并找出我的情况。因此，我认为当你假设每个人都有一个代理人并且这些代理人以这种非常神奇且重要的方式与其他代理人交谈时，整个范式开始发生变化。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: There's a couple more things I want to touch on before we get started, because there's so much to talk about. One is you made this point about SaaS tools not using ... You can use tokens from the model companies basically when using a SaaS tool. Talk a bit more about that, because that may change the business model for SaaS companies in the future. That feels like a big deal.
turns.zh: 在我们开始之前，我还想谈几件事，因为有太多东西要谈。一是您提出了关于 SaaS 工具不使用的观点……您基本上在使用 SaaS 工具时可以使用来自模型公司的代币。多谈谈这一点，因为这可能会改变未来 SaaS 公司的商业模式。这感觉像是一件大事。

turns.speaker: Dan Shipper
turns.en: Well, I think it actually may save their margins, because right now all these companies are rushing to add a agent to their offering and thinking, "Oh, the agent is going to be the main way that people interact with me." And that cost tokens, obviously. And I actually think once I have Codex or Cowork as my main work surface, I still want to use SaaS. So, this is another good prediction. I would buy SaaS stocks right now. I think the SaaS apocalypse is dumb, and SaaS stocks will be up majorly in the next couple years. Not investment advice, but I would buy SaaS stocks. (00:37:25): So, I think it saves your margin because now the way that you're thinking then is not I have to build AI into this, it's more like I have to make a piece of software that humans and AI want to collaborate on together. And that's hard, but once you build it, it's a lot cheaper than assuming everyone's spending tokens, and I think it's a good business. And part of the reason I'm so bullish on SaaS is A, everybody internally here is, like I said, we have all got agents and we're all using Codex and whatever, and we still pay for a ton of SaaS and our SaaS spend is up year over year, and we're not vibe coding every single little thing. And I think that what agents do is increase the number of users of SaaS, not get rid of it. And so, I think SaaS companies are going to see an insane spike in the amount of demand that they have, because there's going to be tons of agents using these products at a very high volume. (00:38:36): And like I said, that's a huge infrastructure challenge. There's a lot of interesting pricing challenges, but it makes me very bullish on SaaS.

turns.en: Automation is a lie, in the sense that every time you automate something, in order to make sure the automation is working well you need a human on top of it making sure that it's working well. And I think there's some differences between being a human manager and being a model manager, but fundamentally it still requires a lot of time and attention. (00:40:07): And I think that we miss that in the model discourse. And one of the reasons is, benchmarks make it look like AI is more autonomous than it is. And by autonomy, I mean something specific by autonomy, and I'm going to try to express this. It's a little hard to express, but I learned this for myself because I've been feeling this paradox a little bit. I've been feeling that we have so much automation, so much AI, and I also work way more. And I think part of the paradox started to resolve for me a little bit when I made my own benchmark. I just vibe coded it on the side while running the rest of Every. (00:41:01): And when we launched it, because it was completely vibe coded, it just started going down and I couldn't fix it and it was very embarrassing. I had a lot of egg on my face. turns.zh: 自动化是一个谎言，从某种意义上说，每次你自动化某件事时，为了确保自动化运行良好，你需要一个人来确保它运行良好。因此，我几年前写了这篇关于分配经济的文章，即人类与人工智能合作的方式就像成为一名经理。关于管理者，你必须记住的一点是，管理者实际上花了很多时间在工作上。大多数经理并不在海滩上，他们一直在与员工沟通并试图弄清楚，“好吧，我们如何让这项工作变得更好？我们如何让它变得更好？它做得怎么样？这个人做得怎么样？”所有这些东西。我认为作为一名人类经理和作为一名模范经理之间存在一些区别，但从根本上来说，它仍然需要大量的时间和注意力。 (00:40:07)：我认为我们在模型讨论中错过了这一点。原因之一是，基准测试让人工智能看起来比实际情况更加自主。说到自治，我指的是自治的具体内容，我将尝试表达这一点。这有点难以表达，但我自己学到了这一点，因为我一直感受到这个悖论。我一直觉得我们有如此多的自动化、如此多的人工智能，而且我的工作量也更多了。我认为当我制定自己的基准时，部分悖论开始为我解决。所以我做了这个高级，它被称为高级工程师基准，就像人工智能与人类工程师相比有多好？我构建它的方式再次是，拥有这个应用程序，Proof。我只是在运行“Every”的其余部分的同时对其进行了编码。 (00:41:01)：当我们推出它时，因为它完全是振动编码的，所以它就开始下降，我无法修复它，这非常尴尬。我脸上沾了很多鸡蛋。该产品有效，我们对其进行了内部测试。我们有很多 Beta 测试人员，但发布后的第二天，服务器就像每隔 10 分钟就会宕机，人们看着我，我会说，“我不知道发生了什么。Codex，修复它。” Codex 的反应是：“我不知道发生了什么。”或者说，Codex 确实是这样的，“我确实知道发生了什么，我已经修复了它。”然后它会导致另外四个错误，然后你只是在原地转圈，而我没有睡觉，而且我感觉编码太难了，以至于我的肘部得了滑囊炎。所以，这里面有一个人生教训。

turns.en: So anyway, I got actually two different senior engineers to fix it independently. So, I have two different rewrites of the code base that tells me how they did it. If you wanted to rewrite it from first principles, how would you rewrite it? Go do it." And mind you, the 60 score was GPT 5.5 using an Opus 4.7 plan. Opus 4.7 plans are very good, GPT 5.5 is the only model though that has the sense of agency and confidence to just like rip out old code and just actually rewrite from first principles. (00:42:48): Other coding models, they end up papering over the edges or around the edges, and they're like, "Oh, this is a big job. I'll just do a little patch." And you're like, "No, I specifically told you not to." So GPT 5.5, there's like a 30 point bump in the score, 60 out of 100. And so for example, it seems like there's no skill or no thought into the prompt, which is this is vibe coder slop. Fix it from first principles. (00:43:41): But actually it took me a while to get to a prompt that didn't give away the answer, but got the model to reveal what it's capable of. And the original prompt I gave it was the original prompt that I gave it when I was trying to fix the issue and production was going down, which is like I had woken up in the morning and I was like, "Okay, we had four or five reported issues yesterday. And if you asked the model, "Hey, should we do that?" It'll probably get there, but it's not going to do it on its own. And there's a lot of incentives pushing against it doing that. And even if it does that, there's always a higher frame for us to go. And so, I think it's really important when we think about benchmark progress to think about it from that perspective, which is benchmarks rise on problems that we've framed that we can articulate, that we can score. (00:45:25): And there's a lot of work that's human work that it can't be scored until you write it down, but the act of thinking to prompt it or write it down is something that you can't measure but means that even if the benchmarks get saturated, it doesn't mean the same thing as you totally replace all senior engineers. And I think it's why even though the models are getting better at automation, I still hire engineers.
turns.zh: 所以无论如何，我实际上有两个不同的高级工程师来独立修复它。因此，我对代码库进行了两种不同的重写，告诉我他们是如何做到的。所以，我要做的就是当我们得到新模型时，我只是给新模型一个提示。我说，“这是振动编码的废话。如果你想从第一原则重写它，你会如何重写它？去做吧。”在 GPT 5.5 之前，所有模型的得分都是 100 分中的 30 分，而人类高级工程师的得分是 100 分中的高 80 分、低 90 分。因此，还有很多工作要做。然后我尝试了 GPT 5.5，它得到了 62 分。请注意，60 分是使用 Opus 4.7 计划的 GPT 5.5。 Opus 4.7 计划非常好，GPT 5.5 是唯一具有代理意识和信心的模型，就像撕掉旧代码并实际上从第一原则重写一样。 (00:42:48)：其他编码模型，他们最终会在边缘或边缘周围贴上纸，然后他们会说，“哦，这是一项艰巨的工作。我只需做一点修补即可。”你会说：“不，我特意告诉过你不要这样做。”因此，GPT 5.5 的分数大约提高了 30 分，满分 100 分是 60 分。很明显，在一年或更短的时间内，它将达到高级工程师级别，这会给您带来一定的印象，特别是根据我命名基准的方式，我认为很多基准都是这样做的。我可以告诉你，当我们到达这一点时，我将很容易更改基准以将当前模型归零，这样就可以在 100 分中得到零。例如，提示似乎没有任何技巧或没有思考，这就是 vivi coder slop。从第一原则解决它。 (00:43:41)：但实际上我花了一段时间才得到一个提示，该提示没有给出答案，但让模型揭示了它的能力。我给它的最初提示是当我试图解决问题而生产下降时我给它的最初提示，就像我早上醒来一样，我想，“好吧，我们昨天报告了四五个问题。我希望你仔细检查所有问题，然后制定一个如何解决所有问题的计划，然后去做。”市场上的每个编码模型，我很确定......这是一个预测，我很确定市场上的每个编码模型在一年内仍然会这样做。市场上的每个编码模型都会认真对待该指令。 (00:44:32)：如果我告诉它，“这里有很多问题，去解决它”，他们就会去尝试解决这些问题。真正的人类高级工程师所做的就是他们查看代码库，然后他们会说，“这就是一坨狗屎。这个家伙不知道他在做什么。”然后他们说，“我们实际上必须重写很多内容，这将是困难和冒险的。我知道你们都想听这个，但我们必须这样做。”如果你问模型，“嘿，我们应该这样做吗？”它可能会到达那里，但它不会自己做到这一点。有很多激励因素阻碍它这样做。即使做到了这一点，我们总有一个更高的框架可以去。因此，我认为，当我们考虑基准进展时，从这个角度思考它是非常重要的，即基准的上升是基于我们已经提出的问题，我们可以阐明，我们可以评分。 (00:45:25)：有很多工作是人类的工作，除非你把它写下来，否则无法对其进行评分，但是提示它或写下来的思考行为是你无法衡量的，但这意味着即使基准达到饱和，这并不意味着你完全取代了所有高级工程师。我认为这就是为什么即使模型在自动化方面越来越好，我仍然雇用工程师。

turns.speaker: Dan Shipper
turns.en: There's all this interesting stuff in terms of the shape of work. Once you're in this land where you've got async agents off that you delegate work to, then you've got your Codex Claude Code work surface that starts to happen. So one thing that we see a lot internally, and you also see this in the big model companies, is the number of pull requests that you get is like skyrockets. We have people in consulting or in ops roles or whatever or editors just making pull requests. And A, that's really cool and that's a very different shape of work where you can expect that a higher percentage of your company or your users are going to be doing things that previously only technical users can do. And what that does is it creates all this pressure on the other end for the people who have to deal with all of the new code for how to deal with that. (00:51:26): And so I think there's a lot of interesting things that happen with that. So for example, like OpenClaw, I mentioned that earlier. Pete gets thousands of poll requests a day on OpenClaw and then he just spins up 50,000 Codex instances and then sorts through them and then merges a thousand of them. It's really crazy. I actually think that that's going to be more and more common. (00:51:55): It brings up a lot of really interesting questions around which poll requests should you merge. And whenever you add capacity in one part of your process, it breaks things. It used to be really hard to build things and now it's very easy. So the point is not, can we build it? It's like, would it make sense with the rest of what we've built and how do we keep a sense of a coherent whole. And also, what do we delete? I think Anthropic does this really well. They delete a lot of stuff from Claude Code to make sure that it's not bloated. So I think there's a lot of that going to happen on one side. There's a lot of non-technical people can do technical work and then technical people are in charge of making sure that that work gets into a product or into a process in a cohesive, coherent way. (00:52:47): And also their product people are going to be doing that too. And I think that's quite cool.
turns.zh: 就工作的形式而言，有很多有趣的东西。一旦您进入这片土地，您可以将工作委派给异步代理，那么您就可以开始使用 Codex Claude Code 工作界面了。因此，我们在内部经常看到的一件事，你也可以在大型模型公司中看到这一点，那就是你收到的拉取请求的数量就像猛增一样。我们有担任咨询或运营角色或其他职位的人，或者编辑只是提出拉取请求。 A，这真的很酷，这是一种非常不同的工作形式，您可以期望公司或用户中更高比例的人将做以前只有技术用户才能做的事情。这样做的结果是，它给另一端的人们带来了所有这些压力，他们必须处理所有新代码以了解如何处理这些问题。 (00:51:26)：所以我认为这会发生很多有趣的事情。例如，像 OpenClaw，我之前提到过。 Pete 每天在 OpenClaw 上收到数千个投票请求，然后他只需启动 50,000 个 Codex 实例，然后对它们进行排序，然后合并其中的一千个。真的很疯狂。事实上，我认为这种情况会越来越普遍。 (00:51:55)：它提出了许多非常有趣的问题，围绕您应该合并哪些民意调查请求。每当您在流程的某一部分增加容量时，就会破坏事情。过去建造东西真的很难，但现在却非常容易。所以重点不是，我们能建造它吗？就像，它对我们所构建的其他内容有意义吗？我们如何保持一个连贯的整体感。另外，我们要删除什么？我认为 Anthropic 在这方面做得非常好。他们从 Claude Code 中删除了很多内容，以确保它不会臃肿。所以我认为一方面会发生很多事情。有很多非技术人员可以做技术工作，然后技术人员负责确保这些工作以一种有凝聚力、连贯的方式进入产品或流程。 (00:52:47)：他们的产品人员也会这样做。我认为这很酷。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Something I'm hearing from people is that now that everyone can do everything, like engineers can design, PMs can code, marketing people can ship stuff. There's just this confusion about what the hell is my job anymore. What am I responsible for exactly? Am I supposed to be shipping stuff? Am I still a marketing person? And it's just creating a lot of confusion and certainty in the world, just a comment.
turns.zh: 我从人们那里听到的是，现在每个人都可以做任何事情，比如工程师可以设计，产品经理可以编码，营销人员可以运送东西。人们对我的工作到底是什么感到困惑。我具体负责什么？我应该去运送东西吗？我还是一个营销人吗？它只是在世界上制造了很多混乱和确定性，只是一个评论。

turns.speaker: Dan Shipper
turns.en: I mean, it's for real. And one of the things that I think is special about every is... Everyone is sort of a generalist and really loves having their fingers in a lot of different pots or whatever the metaphor is. I think that'll probably settle down at some point and it'll feel more normal. Marketing people are still going to do marketing even if they're touching the website. That's just part of marketing now. But I also think that you can get a lot further being a generalist now and that's like really cool, especially for smaller companies. The other thing that I think is interesting is there are definitely some new job roles that are a thing. (00:53:52): And the thing that is becoming really clear is the whole Ford deployed engineer concept I think is for real and it comes out of every agent needs a human. You go to the big model companies, they have these agents that run internally, they have like teams of people that run these agents and I don't think those teams are going away. The models are going to get more powerful, the agents are going to get more powerful and the number of agents is going to grow, but people are still going to manage them. And so that looks like a very specific kind of person. And we have a couple of those people internally here and it's like the people who are in charge of making sure your agents are working and doing the right thing. We also do consulting. So we lend that out to people and I think that's a big thing that people want. (00:54:44): And it's another one of those places where you're like, hmm, automation was supposed to take away jobs, but it looks like it just created one or many. (00:54:53): And there's a specific type of engineer that really loves... Nitesh, who fits this, he's an AI engineer and he fits this sort of forward deployed category and he's on our team. He spends most of his time actually talking to one of our agents in Slack. We have an agent internally called Claudy, which runs our whole consulting practice and he spends a lot of time in Slack. There is code and he is using Claude Code and other things like that, but a lot of it is just talking to it and being like, "Why did you do this dumb thing? Let's fix that." And so there's certain kinds of engineers that I think love that and love having their hands on the latest thing and also love making this being that's in a workspace and it looks a bit different than more traditional, building more traditional software.
turns.zh: 我的意思是，这是真的。我认为每个人的特别之处之一是......每个人都是多面手，并且非常喜欢将手指放在许多不同的罐子或任何隐喻中。我认为这种情况可能会在某个时候稳定下来，并且感觉会更加正常。即使营销人员接触了网站，他们仍然会进行营销。现在这只是营销的一部分。但我也认为，现在你可以成为一名多面手，这真的很酷，特别是对于小公司来说。我认为有趣的另一件事是肯定有一些新的工作角色。 (00:53:52)：现在变得非常清晰的是整个福特部署工程师的概念，我认为这是真实的，它源于每个代理都需要一个人。你去大型模特公司，他们有内部运行的代理，他们有类似的团队来管理这些代理，我不认为这些团队会消失。模型将会变得更加强大，代理将会变得更加强大，代理的数量将会增加，但人们仍然会管理它们。所以这看起来是一种非常特殊的人。我们内部有一些这样的人，他们就像负责确保您的代理正在工作并做正确的事情的人。我们也做咨询。所以我们把它借给人们，我认为这是人们想要的一件大事。 (00:54:44)：这是另一个你会想的地方，嗯，自动化应该会夺走工作岗位，但看起来它只是创造了一个或多个工作岗位。 (00:54:53)：有一种特定类型的工程师非常喜欢......Nitesh，他适合这一点，他是一名人工智能工程师，他适合这种前沿部署类别，而且他是我们团队的一员。他大部分时间都在与我们在 Slack 中的一位客服人员进行实际交谈。我们有一位内部代理，名叫 Claudy，负责管理我们的整个咨询业务，他在 Slack 上花费了大量时间。有代码，他正在使用克劳德代码和其他类似的东西，但很多只是与它交谈，然后说，“你为什么要做这个愚蠢的事情？让我们解决这个问题。”因此，我认为某些类型的工程师喜欢这一点，喜欢掌握最新的东西，也喜欢在工作空间中制作这个东西，它看起来与更传统的、构建更传统的软件有点不同。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: And your sense there is we're not near a place where these agents don't need a human. You've said that so many times now that agents need a human and there's kind of like the setup part and then there's the maintaining it forever part and feels like both are important. Is what I'm hearing like this is going to be a job for a long time. AI is not going to get smart enough to just be fully automated for a while.
turns.zh: 你的感觉是我们还没有接近这些特工不需要人类的地方。您已经说过很多次了，代理需要人工，有点像设置部分，然后是永久维护部分，感觉两者都很重要。我听说这将是一份很长一段时间的工作。人工智能暂时还不会变得足够聪明，无法实现完全自动化。

turns.speaker: Dan Shipper
turns.en: Yes. I'm simultaneously extremely AI-pilled, extremely, and very bullish on humans and the role of humans and making sure that AI is working well.
turns.zh: 是的。同时，我对人工智能非常着迷，非常非常看好人类和人类的角色，并确保人工智能运转良好。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Interesting. Okay. So the two kind of buckets here that you're talking about, one is like the way I think I hear what you described earlier is just the pace of shipping software and everything is just increasing, which also means there's so much more work reviewing all this sloppy output. I was just talking to a data science friend and he was saying how his team is just, his data science team is just, their job used to be do analysis, answer questions, see if this experiment was a good, was positive. Now it's just everyone's doing that and they're sharing their results and they're like, "No, this is not correct." And most of their job is now reviewing bad data science work.
turns.zh: 有趣的。好的。所以你在这里谈论的两种桶，一种就像我想我听到你之前描述的那样，只是交付软件的步伐，一切都在增加，这也意味着需要做更多的工作来审查所有这些草率的输出。我刚刚和一位数据科学朋友聊天，他说他的团队是公正的，他的数据科学团队是公正的，他们的工作过去是做分析，回答问题，看看这个实验是否好，是否积极。现在，每个人都在这样做，他们正在分享他们的结果，他们会说，“不，这是不正确的。”他们现在的大部分工作是审查糟糕的数据科学工作。

turns.speaker: Dan Shipper
turns.en: Which is a problem and it means that, and the same thing is happening with engineers and it means that you need more, like you actually need that engineers for this and you need data scientists and it means that you haven't set up the appropriate systems or agents to help you with this. So the way that it works inside of the big model companies, for example, at least one of them has literally a data science bot that every single person in the org can query that is hooked up to their data warehouse that knows who's who so that it knows at the warehouse level who has permission to access what. And so all of the basic questions, because there's a team that sets up this bot, all of the basic questions that people might want to ask that it sometimes that might get wrong, that they're constantly making sure it's getting it right. (00:57:42): And so the data science team doesn't have to answer all the bullshit questions because there's another team building an agent that is set up to do that really well. But if the team didn't exist, the data scientists would hate their lives.
turns.zh: 这是一个问题，这意味着，同样的事情也发生在工程师身上，这意味着你需要更多，就像你实际上需要工程师，你需要数据科学家，这意味着你还没有建立适当的系统或代理来帮助你解决这个问题。例如，它在大型模型公司内部的工作方式，例如，至少其中一家拥有一个数据科学机器人，组织中的每个人都可以查询该机器人，该机器人连接到他们的数据仓库，该数据仓库知道谁是谁，以便在仓库级别知道谁有权访问什么。所以所有的基本问题，因为有一个团队设置了这个机器人，人们可能想问的所有基本问题，有时可能会出错，他们不断确保它是正确的。 (00:57:42)：因此数据科学团队不必回答所有废话问题，因为还有另一个团队正在构建一个代理，该代理的设置可以很好地做到这一点。但如果这个团队不存在，数据科学家们就会讨厌他们的生活。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Yeah. It does though make the job maybe less fun because you're just sitting there gardening people's sloppy work versus-
turns.zh: 是的。但这确实会让这项工作变得不那么有趣，因为你只是坐在那里照顾人们草率的工作，而不是——

turns.speaker: Dan Shipper
turns.en: Well, that's what I think is like it can actually make the job better because for the data scientists, you are now not dealing with all the silly requests. You're dealing with the deeper questions that are harder for the team who's dealing with all the basic requests and building an agent to do that. It's like filtering all that stuff out so you can focus.
turns.zh: 嗯，我认为这实际上可以让工作变得更好，因为对于数据科学家来说，你现在不需要处理所有愚蠢的请求。您正在处理更深层次的问题，对于处理所有基本请求并建立代理来完成此任务的团队来说，这些问题更加困难。这就像过滤掉所有这些东西，这样你就可以集中注意力。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Here's a question I've been thinking about. I was not planning to talk about this, but it's something that I've been thinking about. So the question is which product tech role is the least changed now? So engineers, 100% of code AI now. It's like a completely different job. Product management, a lot of the PRDs are, you don't have to write as much, you can ship code, you don't have to wait for people. Design, the whole design process dead according to recent guests, just like there's no time to do the whole design process, very different role. Data science, very different work now. There's marketing, there's sales. So here's the question, what do you think is the least fundamentally changed role so far?
turns.zh: 这是我一直在思考的一个问题。我原本不打算谈论这个，但这是我一直在思考的事情。那么问题是现在哪个产品技术角色变化最小？所以工程师们，现在100%都是AI代码。这就像一份完全不同的工作。产品管理，很多PRD都是，不用写那么多，可以发货代码，不用等人。设计，整个设计过程死了，根据最近的客人，就像没有时间做整个设计过程一样，角色很不一样。数据科学，现在的工作截然不同。有营销，就有销售。那么问题来了，你认为迄今为止最没有根本改变的角色是什么？

turns.speaker: Dan Shipper
turns.en: Well, on interesting thing is, I don't know if this counts, but CEOs and investors, it seems still very, very optional whether or not they use this stuff. It seems that way. I think the opposite is actually true. My experience, and we do a lot of this with senior executives and senior leadership teams, my experience is that your company's only going to go as far as your CEO goes in AI and it's not something you can delegate. You have to have your hands in it because otherwise you don't have an intuition for it. But for a long time it has seemed like, yeah, that's something that the people who are doing the work have to do, but I don't have to do that. I'll just tell them what to do. And so I think if you're a CEO, you kind of can get away with your day looking very similar. (00:59:54): I think that will change rapidly at some point where it'll be like, "Oh no, I'm way behind." But for now, or maybe even middle managers, those kinds of people, I think it's fairly similar. I think maybe sales because it's so in person.
turns.zh: 有趣的是，我不知道这是否重要，但是首席执行官和投资者，是否使用这些东西似乎仍然非常非常可选。看来是这样。我认为事实恰恰相反。根据我的经验，我们与高级管理人员和高级领导团队做了很多这样的事情，我的经验是，你的公司只能在人工智能方面走得更远，这不是你可以委托的事情。你必须亲自动手，否则你就没有直觉。但很长一段时间以来，似乎，是的，这是从事这项工作的人必须做的事情，但我不必这样做。我只会告诉他们该怎么做。所以我认为，如果你是一名首席执行官，你的一天可能会看起来非常相似。 (00:59:54)：我认为这种情况会在某个时候迅速改变，就像“哦，不，我远远落后了。”但就目前而言，甚至可能是中层管理人员，这类人，我认为这是相当相似的。我想也许是销售，因为它是如此面对面。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Yeah, that's my vote.
turns.zh: 是的，这是我的投票。

turns.speaker: Dan Shipper
turns.en: It's sort of creeping up in the kind of BDR. We can deal with a lot of BDR type queries. You're only talking to people who actually want it. For sales, it's so useful to do research. My favorite Codex, one of my favorite Codex experiences is we're hiring a head of L&D and we always put out a job post, whatever, but I was like, "I feel like there's this company called General Assembly in New York and they've done really good technology education for a long time." And so I was like, "I feel like someone who worked at General Assembly and is now into AI would be really good." And I just literally typed it into Codex and then went off and was doing something else and I came back and it found this the perfect guy. It was like worked at General Assembly, was an instructor, is super AI-pilled and follows me on Twitter. (01:01:17): So I just DM'd him and then I had dinner with him and it's like, that's crazy. That would've taken so long before and super valuable for sales, for recruiting, all that kind of stuff.
turns.zh: 它有点像 BDR 那样悄然兴起。我们可以处理很多BDR类型的查询。您只与真正想要它的人交谈。对于销售来说，进行研究非常有用。我最喜欢的 Codex，我最喜欢的 Codex 体验之一是我们正在招聘一名 L&D 负责人，我们总是发布一个工作职位，无论如何，但我当时想，“我觉得纽约有一家名为 General Assembly 的公司，他们长期以来一直在做非常好的技术教育。”所以我想，“我觉得在 General Assembly 工作过、现在进入人工智能领域的人会非常好。”我只是将其直接输入 Codex，然后就去做其他事情，然后我回来发现这是一个完美的人。就像在 General Assembly 工作一样，是一名讲师，拥有超级 AI 功能，并且在 Twitter 上关注我。 (01:01:17)：所以我直接给他发了私信，然后我和他一起吃了晚饭，感觉这太疯狂了。这在以前会花费很长时间，而且对于销售、招聘等所有这些事情来说都非常有价值。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Yeah. Sales is where my mind went. The top of funnel AI is helping a lot with sourcing and qualifying things like that. It feels like the work of a salesperson is not fundamentally different and (01:01:39): Customer support's fundamentally changed. So that's interesting. Sales so far so good for those folks. Okay. So maybe just summarizing some of the predictions in this bucket of just the shape of the work, how it's going to change. What I'm hearing so far is just going to be a lot more reviewing of other people's output as a part of the work. And then two, there's going to be a lot of like almost babysitting of AI agents to make them do the thing you want them to do for deploying and then just gardening them along the way, make sure they continue to do their work. Anything else before we get into our third bucket?
turns.zh: 是的。销售是我的心思所在。漏斗人工智能的顶部在采购和鉴定此类事情方面提供了很大帮助。感觉销售人员的工作并没有本质上的不同（01:01:39）：客户支持发生了根本性的变化。这很有趣。到目前为止，销售情况对这些人来说还不错。好的。所以也许只是总结一下这方面的一些预测，即工作的形式，它将如何改变。到目前为止，我所听到的只是将更多地审查其他人的输出作为工作的一部分。第二，将会有很多类似人工智能代理的保姆，让他们做你希望他们做的部署事情，然后一路照顾他们，确保他们继续做他们的工作。在我们进入第三个桶之前还有什么吗？

turns.speaker: Dan Shipper
turns.en: I would sort of split it into less babysitting agents and more your forward deployed team is trying to build a whole system that makes it so that people who have less knowledge can use that system without doing something dumb. And that's like a really interesting engineering challenge. I think babysitting kind of makes it feel like it's, yeah, you're just kind of waiting for it to fuck up and then fixing it or whatever. And that can be the case, but I think a lot of it is this extremely interesting engineering challenge of building a system to enable everybody else in your organization to do what used to be a technical job. And then if you're not one of those people, like you're the data scientist or whatever, you can go a lot deeper with AI into really important questions that eventually probably filter into the work that the forward deployed engineering team is doing, but is like more generative and more new and you're dealing with harder questions. One last thing that I think is really interesting is I think that we will be reading way more AI generated writing in documents and emails and we will like it. (01:03:20): And I think we are already doing this in coding where we read plan documents. I don't want an engineer to hand write a plan document. That would be very silly. It would be obviously silly. And I think the same is true when we did our quarterly planning for every at the end of 2025, we did it all with Notion Agents and we just had a bunch of Notion agents and we had really one Notion agent and then we had a top level company strategy and then we had everybody in the company just talked to an agent and it asked them about what happened last year, how did it go, what were your goals? What do you want to do this year? What are your metrics? It pushed back and then it was like, how does this relate to the overall company idea? All that kind of stuff. (01:04:10): And then I got these incredibly good AI generated strategy reports or quarterly plans for each part of each team. And then I could go in and be like, "Okay, who needs to talk to each other? Which teams need to talk to each other that don't know they need to talk to each other? And which one of these is actually low quality or which one of these is high quality?" All that kind of stuff, it makes it a lot easier to process. And I see that all the time now. I consistently get AI generated stuff and there's a difference between an AI generated document that's slop and not. And the slap one is it took them less time to make it than it takes me to read it and they don't stand behind every line. So my expectation is if you send me an AI generated document, I think that's great. And if we talk about it and it's clear you have no idea what's in it, big no-no, not allowed to do that. And I think we have this aversion to AI-generated stuff that will go away because the kind of strategy document that GBT 5.5 can write when it's directed well by someone on my team is way better than them just like dinking and dunking their fingers on the keyboard.
turns.zh: 我会把它分成更少的保姆代理，更多的是你的前沿部署团队正在尝试构建一个完整的系统，以便知识较少的人可以使用该系统而无需做一些愚蠢的事情。这就像一个非常有趣的工程挑战。我认为保姆有点让人感觉，是的，你只是在等待它搞砸，然后修复它或其他什么。情况可能是这样，但我认为很大程度上是这个极其有趣的工程挑战，即构建一个系统，使组织中的其他人能够完成以前的技术工作。然后，如果你不是这些人中的一员，比如你是数据科学家或其他什么人，你可以利用人工智能更深入地研究真正重要的问题，这些问题最终可能会渗透到前沿部署的工程团队正在做的工作中，但就像更具生成性和更新性一样，你正在处理更困难的问题。我认为真正有趣的最后一件事是，我认为我们将阅读更多由人工智能生成的文档和电子邮件写作，我们会喜欢它。 (01:03:20)：我认为我们已经在阅读计划文档的编码中这样做了。我不希望工程师手写计划文件。那将是非常愚蠢的。这显然是愚蠢的。我认为当我们在 2025 年底为每个人制定季度计划时也是如此，我们都是通过 Notion Agents 完成的，我们只有一群 Notion 代理，我们真的有一个 Notion 代理，然后我们有一个顶级公司战略，然后我们让公司里的每个人都与代理交谈，询问他们去年发生了什么，进展如何，你的目标是什么？今年你想做什么？你的指标是什么？它反驳道，然后就想，这与公司的整体理念有什么关系？所有这些东西。 (01:04:10)：然后我得到了这些非常好的人工智能为每个团队的每个部分生成的战略报告或季度计划。然后我可以进去说，“好吧，谁需要互相交谈？哪些团队需要互相交谈，但他们不知道自己需要互相交谈？其中哪一个实际上是低质量的，或者哪一个是高质量的？”所有这些东西，它使它更容易处理。我现在经常看到这一点。我一直收到人工智能生成的东西，人工智能生成的文档之间是有区别的。最令人遗憾的是，他们制作这本书所花费的时间比我阅读它所花费的时间还要少，而且他们并不支持每一行。所以我的期望是，如果您向我发送人工智能生成的文档，我认为那就太好了。如果我们谈论它，很明显你不知道里面有什么，这是大禁忌，不允许这样做。我认为我们对人工智能生成的东西的这种厌恶将会消失，因为在我团队中某人的指导下，GBT 5.5 可以编写的那种策略文档比他们更好，就像在键盘上敲击手指一样。

turns.zh: 我们也有这个用于外部物品。我们发布所有这些指南，这些指南通常是代理，它们是代理协助的，代理是合著者，它们旨在供人类和代理阅读。那是因为如果你正在写大量信息，我的意思是，你会一直这样做。 (01:07:47)：为了真正应用它，最好的方法就是让你的代理吸收它，并记住下次我进行定价时提醒我本指南，我们将一起浏览它或其他什么。它可以让您更好地实施想法，并且可以让您更深入地了解，因为代理可以在一秒钟内阅读大约 10,000 页。因此，您与人类谈论故事、重要的事情以及核心思想，代理拥有所有细节，然后在您需要时可以为您应用。

turns.zh: 我非常非常看好产品经理。我知道你的观众可能会喜欢这一点，但我的轶事让我确信这一点是我们内部有这个人。他的名字叫马库斯，他运营着 Spiral，这是我们的写作应用程序。马库斯是一位受过培训的产品经理。他之前负责 Axios 的写作产品，担任 PM，拥有一支庞大的团队，ARR 收入达到数千万。他从那份工作中辞职了一年，刚刚获得了超级人工智能的帮助，并且学会了如何基本上很好地使用光标。现在我认为他使用了Claude Code，但他的光标被严重迷惑了很长一段时间。我会称他为轻度技术人员，就像知道什么是数据库迁移一样。如果他必须看代码，我认为他能理解，但即使在一年前，我们也根本不可能雇用他来做这项工作，但编码模型已经足够好，他可以将他所拥有的技术知识与他真正敏锐的产品意识、写作意识和用户意识结合起来，这是非常危险的。 (01:10:01)：他的发货速度比团队中的几乎任何人都快，而且他对每一个用户、每一次对话都非常关注，比如这意味着什么，我们如何将其收集到一个关于我们下一步想要去哪里的故事中，以及我们需要解决哪些问题？诸如此类的事情。我认为他感到自由，因为他不需要组织整个团队来做到这一点。他就可以做到。这是非常令人印象深刻的，这让我非常非常看好任何真正被人工智能包围的 PM。

And that's the exact thing that it's really hard to do with vibe coding because it just all looks the same. So it all looks like Slap and they can make stuff that looks so different and now they can actually build it. (01:11:51): And what you see when we work with them internally is now they're just making pull requests. They don't need to hand it off as much. Sometimes they do, but a lot of times they just make pull requests and-
turns.zh: 好的。因此，我认为其他人将成为超级、超级力量的人，这是因为我们在内部看到了这一点，他们是全栈设计师。如果你是一名设计师，并且一直使用这些工具，那么你已经习惯了，好吧，我做出了这种美妙的交互，而工程师只是不想这样做，或者它没有按照我认为应该发生的方式发生，或者有所有这些东西，我看到我们内部或外部的很多设计师，他们现在觉得自己有能力去构建东西，因为他们就像，“我有所有这些想法，让事情看起来很棒，还有这些有趣的交互。”这正是 Vivi 编码很难做到的事情，因为它看起来都一样。所以这一切看起来都像 Slap，他们可以制造看起来如此不同的东西，现在他们可以实际建造它。 (01:11:51)：当我们在内部与他们合作时，您会看到他们现在只是发出拉取请求。他们不需要那么多的交接。有时他们会这样做，但很多时候他们只是提出拉取请求，然后-

turns.en: ... Need to hand it off as much. Sometimes they do, but a lot of times they just make pull requests and it's like the thing is built and that's it. turns.zh: ...需要尽可能多地交出它。有时他们会这样做，但很多时候他们只是提出拉取请求，就好像东西已经构建好了，仅此而已。我认为这对于公司的运作方式来说是不可思议的，但这些人也有一个巨大的机会成为企业家并开始自己的事业，因为他们现在可以制造东西。我认为设计师都是非常有创造力的人，我认为人工智能对于任何这样的人来说都是一个超级工具。
